editorial.headline: Early-Childhood Playgroups, Open Nationally and in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers organised playgroup and preschool education for young children, with foreign investment open nationally and a clear path for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
Playgroup education is an early-childhood education activity for children aged two to six, with priority given to ages three and four. Its centre is the playgroup itself, whether managed by government or by the community. The scope also includes preschool education that combines educational and child-welfare programmes from birth through age six, with priority for children aged two to four. It is a clearly defined setting for early-years learning and care.

The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as the scales open to this activity. It also expressly includes playgroups formed through cooperation with foreign educational institutions. Within the formal education route described, that cooperation joins a foreign educational institution accredited or recognised in its own country with an Indonesian educational institution, in line with applicable legal provisions. The defining subject remains the playgroup and preschool education activity set out in the scope.

Nationally, PMA status is open, with a maximum foreign ownership level of 100%. Put plainly, the record allows full foreign ownership for this activity at the national level; it does not set a national foreign-share cap below that level. That openness is not detached from the activity’s stated form: cooperation involving foreign educational institutions is expressly included in the scope. The educational focus, however, remains early-childhood provision for the children and age ranges described.

Bali’s position is also open on the facts supplied. The local status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is not blocked by the moratorium. The reason is specific: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi—medium-high/high—which keeps it outside the stated moratorium block. A foreign investor can therefore register this activity in Bali today. The local result follows the recorded risk treatment at the Besar scale, while the national ownership ceiling remains 100%.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this early-childhood education activity in Bali today, with national ownership open to 100%.
